learning_outcomes.text: Student has a basic knowledge about: laws in DC and AC circuits, electronic elements, systems of electricity production
Student has a basic knowledge about: control systems of electrical machines, actuators and measurement devices.
Student has a basic knowledge about: induction machines, synchronous machines, DC brushed and brushless motors, universal motors, special construction of electromechanical converters

Students know: how measure and calculate parameters and characteristics of induction motor, how measure and calculate parameters characteristics of synchronous machine, how the PWM converter works with induction motor, how measure and calculate parameters and characteristics of DC motor, how measure and calculate parameters and characteristics of 1-phase induction motors

Students know: how to use measurement devices, how to measure and calculate basic parameters of DC and AC circuits, how to measure and calculate basic parameters of 3-phase AC circuit, how measure and calculate parameters of transformer,
Student is able to work in group and knows the importance of power system for economy and industry

syllabus_topics: Module A and B: Measurements id DC circuits, winding and insulation resistance.
Measurements and analysis of 1-phase induction motor.
Measurements and analysis of mechanical properties of DC servomotors.
Module C: Measurements id DC circuits, winding and insulation resistance.
Measurements and analysis of induction machine based on Kloss’s formula, work with PWM converter.
Measurements and analysis of synchronous machine.
Measurements and analysis of mechanical properties of DC motors.
Instantaneous power in electrical circuits. Active power. Voltage and current Kirchhoff’s laws. Thevenin’s principle. DC circuits.
Magnetic circuits. Permanent magnets. Ampere’s law. 1-phase transformer. Saturation and hysteresis.
AC circuits. Active, reactive and apparent power.
Symbolic method. Phasor diagrams. Transient and steady state in R+L+C circuits. Series and parallel resonance. Laplace transform.
Three-phase circuits. Wye and delta configuration. Power in 3-phase circuits.
Measuring instruments. Ammeter, voltmeter and wattmeter for DC and AC applications.

Electromechanical energy conversion. Synchronous machines: motors and generators. Phasor diagram. Induction machine. Steady-state torque versus speed characteristics. Capacitor motor. Induction servo motor. Commutator machines. Series, shunt and separate excitation. AC commutator motors. Brushless DC motors. Stepper motors.
Power electronic elements. Static converters for speed adjustable drives.Speed and positions indicators. Resolvers. Encoders. Piezoelectric motors and actuators.
teaching_methods: Visual thinking (mind mapping, concept mapping, sketchnoting)
assessment_rules: To receive a positive evaluation of laboratory exercises (Mlab) it is necessary to perform all laboratory exercises and obtain positive grades from passing reports of all laboratory exercises. The mark (Mlab) is determined based on the arithmetic average of the marks of reports. In case of a negative grade for Mlab, improvement is possible via a correction test. The grade for the lecture test (Mtest) is determined based on the final test result. The final grade (Mfinal) is determined by the algorithm: Mfinal = 0.5*Mlab + 0.5*Mtest. To obtain a positive Mfinal, it is necessary to obtain positive grades from all laboratory exercises (Mlab) and the lecture test (Mtest).
